Hi! I can help you. 

Look at the bottom numbers. 

We have 3 and 6. 

How do we get from 3 to 6? 

What do we multiply by?
Is it 2/6? I honestly do not get this at all, it makes no sense.

That is okay! Fractions can be hard. 

Let us look again. 

To go from 3 to 6, we times by 2. 

Whatever we do to the bottom, we must do to the top. 

Can you times the top number, 2, by 2?
Oh, I get it now. It is 4/6 because 2 times 2 is 4. Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

Well done! You got it right. 

Now we are adding fractions. 

Look at the bottom numbers. They are both 9. 

When the bottom numbers are the same, they stay the same. 

So the bottom of our answer is 9. 

Now, add the top numbers. What is 2 plus 4?
is it 6/18 because you add the 9 and 9 together at the bottom

Not quite! 

When we add fractions, the bottom number stays the same. 

It does not change. 

So the bottom number is 9. 

Now look at the top numbers. 

What is 2 plus 4?

Yes! 6/9 is right. 

You are doing so well. 

Now we have 1/4 plus 1/8. 

The bottom numbers are different. 

They are 4 and 8. 

Can you change 1/4 so the bottom is 8? 

What do you times 4 by to get 8?
Wait, do I just add the top numbers and bottom numbers? Is it 2/12? I hate when the denominators are different.

I know, different bottoms are tricky. 

No, we do not add them. 

We must make the bottoms the same first. 

To turn 4 into 8, we times by 2. 

Can you times the top number, 1, by 2?
